**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 8, §8.2. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

To choose parameters, define a loss measuring bad predictions and minimise average loss on observed training records. The optimisation objective is explicit and reproducible.

## Formal relationship

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol\theta}=\arg\min_{\boldsymbol\theta}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(f_{\boldsymbol\theta}(\boldsymbol x_i),y_i)
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

Two candidate predictions for observed y=12 are 11 and 9. Squared errors are (11-12)^2=1 and (9-12)^2=9. ERM prefers the first on that record; the full objective aggregates all training records.

## Interpretation and limitations

Empirical risk approximates expected population risk only under sampling assumptions. Regularisation adds an explicit penalty to control complexity: Ltrain(theta)+lambda Omega(theta).
